problem: Federated learning systems struggle to personalize models when clients have heterogeneous computational resources and data distributions, because personalized and generalized knowledge often interfere with each other.
approach: FedEMoE proposes an Elastic Mixture of Experts architecture that decouples personalization from generalization by using personalized experts for multi-scale feature extraction and an elastic shared expert that adapts to expert heterogeneity via weight spectrum analysis.
contribution: FedEMoE significantly improves accuracy on heterogeneous models across statistical and model heterogeneity settings.

problem: Converting pre-trained dense LLMs to sparse Mixture-of-Experts architectures for inference efficiency is unstable and typically relies on heuristic clustering or random splitting of feed-forward networks.
approach: DOT-MoE formulates expert decomposition as a Differentiable Optimal Transport problem, using Sinkhorn-Knopp iterations to enforce strict capacity constraints and Straight-Through Estimators to jointly learn neuron-to-expert assignment and routing end-to-end.
contribution: DOT-MoE retains 90% of dense model performance while reducing active parameters by 50%, outperforming structured pruning and heuristic clustering baselines.

problem: Deepfake detection methods that reconstruct real content via continuous manifold modeling (e.g., VAEs, diffusion models) may inadvertently enable interpolation of forgery artifacts, creating ambiguity in detection.
approach: The method discretizes the real latent manifold by incorporating learnable vector quantization into CLIP's feature space while adding adaptive tangent space projection for continuous relaxation, balancing discrete constraints with generalization.
contribution: The approach achieves robust deepfake detection on diverse datasets through tighter latent space constraints combined with controlled continuous relaxation.

problem: Unsupervised skill discovery in reinforcement learning typically requires action labels, rewards, or manual annotations, limiting applicability to complex environments.
approach: A grammar-based hierarchical approach segments unlabeled trajectories into skills and induces hierarchical structure without requiring annotations, capturing both low-level behaviors and their compositional combinations.
contribution: The method produces more structured and semantically meaningful skill hierarchies than baselines in pixel-based environments including Minecraft, and accelerates downstream RL tasks.

problem: Autonomous LLM fine-tuning for domain-specific applications remains labor-intensive, requiring manual data curation, training configuration, and iterative diagnosis of model behavior.
approach: FT-Dojo provides an interactive benchmark environment with 13 tasks across 5 domains and a standardized task interface, while FT-Agent uses structured iteration planning, fail-fast validation, and multi-level feedback to autonomously refine data and training strategies.
contribution: FT-Agent achieves best performance on 10 out of 13 FT-Dojo tasks and demonstrates autonomous recovery from failures through cumulative learning.

problem: Instruction-based image editing quality depends heavily on carefully designed instructions, placing the burden of task decomposition and sequencing on users.
approach: PhotoAgent formulates autonomous image editing as a long-horizon decision-making problem, using tree search to plan multi-step editing actions and closed-loop execution with visual feedback and memory, without requiring step-by-step user prompts.
contribution: PhotoAgent significantly outperforms existing methods in instruction faithfulness and visual quality across diverse editing scenarios.

problem: Causal softmax attention in language models is restricted to coarse scalar forget gates, but fine-grained element-wise gates show superior effectiveness yet are difficult to integrate due to algebraic constraints.
approach: FiX introduces element-wise forget gates into softmax attention by reformulating the mechanism as element-wise multiplication on value vectors after recognizing that the softmax denominator becomes redundant under subsequent RMSNorm, enabling the first positional encoding applied to value-output pairs.
contribution: FiX achieves lower training loss and superior performance on short-text benchmarks and long-context tasks compared to scalar-gate approaches.

problem: DDIM inversion for diffusion models inherently accumulates deviations that compound into noticeable inversion errors, and existing methods overlook how timestep selection in the noise scheduler influences inversion fidelity.
approach: The method reveals that deviation scale exhibits a parabolic trend across timesteps and proposes a nonuniform timestep scheduler combining global rescaling with dynamic programming-based rescheduling to minimize overall inversion error.
contribution: The approach consistently improves existing inversion methods with no extra parameters or computational overhead, achieving superior image reconstruction and editing results.

problem: Graph coarsening methods typically preserve either spectral or spatial characteristics while suffering from exponential time complexity, failing to preserve topological features essential for GNN performance.
approach: STPGC introduces graph strong collapse and edge collapse concepts from algebraic topology, eliminating dominated nodes and edges via three algorithms (GStrongCollapse, GEdgeCollapse, NeighborhoodConing) while preserving GNN receptive fields.
contribution: STPGC achieves efficient graph coarsening while rigorously preserving topological features and accelerating GNN training demonstrated on node classification tasks.

problem: Large language models suffer from inherent social biases that cascade through chain-of-thought reasoning in a continuous propagation process, and existing debiasing methods fail to interrupt propagation once triggered.
approach: Self-Debias reformulates debiasing as strategic resource redistribution of output probability mass, using fine-grained trajectory-level optimization subject to dynamic constraints to selectively revise biased suffixes while preserving valid prefixes, plus online self-improvement via consistency filtering.
contribution: With only 20k annotated samples, Self-Debias achieves superior debiasing performance while preserving general reasoning capabilities without continuous external oversight.

problem: Longer chain-of-thought traces and increased review behaviors are assumed to improve reasoning, but the characterization of what makes an effective CoT remains unclear.
approach: The work systematically evaluates CoT effectiveness via a graph view that extracts structure and identifies Failed-Step Fraction (FSF)—the fraction of steps in abandoned branches—as a single statistic that outpredicts length for correctness; interventions include test-time ranking and CoT editing.
contribution: FSF consistently outpredicts length and review ratio for reasoning correctness across ten language models, and removing failed branches significantly improves accuracy.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning for instruction-following induces semantic mode collapse by biasing models toward low-entropy fine-tuning data, degrading the high-entropy semantic diversity of pretraining, particularly at scale.
approach: Annotation-anchored training pretrains on documents with semantic annotations to induce a rich annotation distribution, preserving this distribution during post-training and sampling diverse annotations at inference to guide generation.
contribution: Models trained with annotation-anchored training achieve 6x less diversity collapse than SFT-trained models while improving with scale.

problem: Generating high-quality stereo videos from single-view video sequences requires accurate disparity estimation and scale-aware synthesis.
approach: ImmersePro uses a dual-branch architecture with spatial-temporal attention mechanisms employing implicit disparity guidance to generate stereo pairs without explicit disparity maps, along with a new large-scale YouTube-SBS dataset.
contribution: ImmersePro improves stereo-from-mono baselines by 11.76% (L1), 6.39% (SSIM), and 5.10% (PSNR) on diverse video sequences.

problem: Quantization of Vision-Language Models is assumed to degrade performance, but its broader impact on reliability metrics including calibration, OOD detection, and robustness remains critically under-explored.
approach: A large-scale evaluation (700k runs) characterizes quantization's spectral filtering effect, showing it dampens high-rank spectral components and compels reliance on robust low-rank features.
contribution: Quantization can simultaneously improve accuracy, calibration, OOD detection, and noise robustness in VLMs, enabling deployment of faster, more reliable models.

problem: Simulation environments for robot training lack the diversity, density, and physical complexity of real indoor spaces, limiting policy learning effectiveness.
approach: SceneSmith uses a hierarchical agentic framework with VLM agents (designer, critic, orchestrator) to generate simulation-ready scenes via successive stages from architecture to furniture to object population, integrating text-to-3D synthesis and physical property estimation.
contribution: SceneSmith generates 3-6x more objects than prior methods with <2% collisions and 96% stability, achieving 92% average realism and 91% prompt faithfulness in user studies.

problem: Reparameterization Policy Gradient methods for model-based RL have been restricted to Gaussian policies, failing to leverage recent advances in generative models like flows that could enable better exploration and expressiveness.
approach: RFO realizes the synergy between flow policies and RPG by backpropagating gradients through both flow generation and system dynamics, with tailored regularization for stability and exploration plus action chunking variants.
contribution: RFO achieves almost 2x reward improvement on challenging soft-body locomotion tasks compared to state-of-the-art baselines across rigid, soft bodies with state or visual inputs.

problem: Theoretical understanding of generalization and scaling laws for Mixture-of-Experts Transformers remains limited, particularly how routing combinatorics and active capacity interact.
approach: Theory separates active per-input capacity from routing combinatorics by conditioning on fixed routing patterns and deriving sup-norm covering-number bounds showing metric entropy scales with active parameter budget.
contribution: Results provide a transparent statistical reference point for MoE scaling, clarifying which behaviors are certified by worst-case theory versus arising from routing structure or optimization dynamics.

problem: Understanding how social beliefs evolve in response to major events remains a fundamental challenge, and LLMs lack frameworks to model belief dynamics with interpretability.
approach: Social World Model (SWM) learns state-transition functions for social beliefs by mining temporal patterns and optimizing the evidence lower bound without requiring explicit annotations or census data.
contribution: SWM outperforms time-series foundation models on SWM-bench with 12k+ data points from prediction markets, providing interpretable insights into belief dynamics mechanisms.

problem: Long-context LLM prefilling is bottlenecked by self-attention's quadratic complexity, and existing sparse attention methods use coarse-grained inspection resulting in suboptimal performance.
approach: SALE achieves fine-grained sparse attention via low-bit quantized query-key products approximating attention weights with a novel Relative Attention Score metric, optimized through a custom CUDA kernel with 11% overhead.
contribution: SALE achieves at least 3.36x speedups on Llama-3.1-8B for sequences longer than 64K with negligible accuracy loss, requiring no training and seamless integration.

problem: On-premise small-model deployment for RL alignment is difficult because RL typically requires expensive human annotations or high-quality reward models unsuitable for local settings.
approach: Positive-unlabeled RL distillation queries the teacher once per prompt for an anchor response, samples student candidates locally, and induces pairwise preferences via anchor-conditioned self-ranking to enable local training via preference optimization.
contribution: The method achieves consistently strong performance under low-cost settings without human-labeled preferences or reward models.

problem: Deploying modern models efficiently requires pre-trained models with varying sizes, but conventional pre-training and fine-tuning fail to support flexible architecture adaptation.
approach: SWEET performs constraint-based pre-training to learn a shared weight template and size-specific scalers under Tucker-based factorization, enabling flexible initialization for varying depths and widths via width-wise stochastic scaling.
contribution: SWEET achieves state-of-the-art performance for initializing variable-sized vision models across classification, detection, segmentation, and generation tasks.

problem: Alignment problems like multi-network analysis and multimodal learning increasingly leverage optimal transport but largely overlook principled acquisition of high-quality supervision to improve alignment.
approach: AvAtar quantifies informativeness by measuring gradient-based impact on global alignment results via gradient propagation through entropy-regularized OT, solved efficiently using the adjoint-state method and conjugate gradient descent.
contribution: AvAtar demonstrates effectiveness, scalability, and generalizability on three representative alignment tasks including multimodal and point cloud registration.

problem: Federated causal discovery assumes all clients share the same causal model, but client-specific policies across settings like hospitals naturally induce heterogeneous and unknown interventions.
approach: I-PERI recovers the common CPDAG across clients and orients additional edges by exploiting structural differences induced by interventions, yielding a tighter Φ-Markov Equivalence Class.
contribution: I-PERI provides theoretical convergence guarantees and privacy-preserving properties while recovering causal structure more tightly than assuming homogeneity.

problem: Aligning text-to-image generation with human preferences through RL is computationally expensive, particularly during inference.
approach: Flow-TTRL reinterprets intermediate latent representations as an implicit policy using SDE-based rollouts to explore high-reward trajectories, employing Proximal Reward Difference Prediction for stability and Group Relative Policy Optimization for fine-grained refinement.
contribution: Flow-TTRL elevates Stable Diffusion 3.5-Medium accuracy from 63% to 87% and Flux.1 Dev from 66% to 83% on GenEval, with 15-20% gains across T2I-CompBench without fine-tuning.

problem: Backdoor attacks on federated learning often decay rapidly under repeated aggregation due to difficulty sustaining attack effectiveness across heterogeneous clients.
approach: CTO-VPA aligns trigger-induced representations with aggregation-stable parameter directions by constraining updates to a coupled trigger-parameter subspace discovered via optimization dynamics analysis.
contribution: CTO-VPA achieves substantially improved backdoor persistence and robustness compared to prior attacks across multiple datasets and defense settings.

problem: Large language models contain wide-ranging capabilities but the location and modularity of these capabilities within the model architecture remain unclear.
approach: A compressed sensing method exploits sparsity of task-specific attention heads via strategic knockouts and limited model evaluations to identify necessary components for specific capabilities.
contribution: Zeroing as few as five task-specific heads degrades capability-specific performance by up to 60% while preserving unrelated tasks, revealing modular organization across 1B-14B parameter models.

problem: Final steps of diffusion inversion can degrade sample quality, and this phenomenon's dependence on timestep selection and dimensionality reduction in latent diffusion models is poorly understood.
approach: Analysis under Gaussian framework with linear autoencoders characterizes conditions where early stopping minimizes distance between generated and target distributions, showing interaction between latent dimension and stopping time.
contribution: Lower-dimensional representations benefit from earlier termination while higher-dimensional spaces require later stopping, and autoencoder reconstruction quality serves as a proxy for full LDM performance.

problem: Detecting out-of-distribution samples in diffusion models is challenging, and existing detectors ignore equivariances that diffusion models learn from in-distribution data.
approach: GEPC measures how consistently the learned score transforms under finite groups via a training-free probe, revealing equivariance breaking through Group-Equivariant Posterior Consistency that produces interpretable breaking maps.
contribution: GEPC achieves competitive OOD detection performance compared to recent baselines while remaining computationally lightweight and interpretable on image benchmarks and SAR imagery.

problem: Target network update frequency in Q-learning is treated as a hyperparameter, but principled selection remains poorly understood despite its role in stabilization.
approach: Theoretical analysis through approximate dynamic programming frames periodic Q-learning as nested optimization where each outer iteration applies an inexact Bellman operator approximated by inner optimization.
contribution: Results show constant update schedules are suboptimal with logarithmic sample complexity overhead, and optimal frequency decreases geometrically during learning, enabling principled hyperparameter selection.

problem: Standard contrastive learning minimizes geometric distance assuming strict compactness optimizes discrimination, but this topology-agnostic approach overlooks intrinsic data structure and can cause class confusion under aggressive augmentations.
approach: Topology-Aware Contrastive Learning shifts from geometric singularity to topological connectivity using Persistent Homology to regulate latent space and maintain α-β connectivity balancing cohesion with separability.
contribution: The approach enhances representation quality and reduces augmentation dependence compared to standard baselines with a tighter generalization bound for richer topological connectivity.

problem: Bandit convex optimization with gradient variation suffers from poor dimension dependence in existing methods, particularly for measuring non-consecutive gradient variation.
approach: A refined analysis of non-consecutive gradient variation improves dimension dependence through better understanding of how variation accumulates across bandit queries.
contribution: Results improve bounds for both convex and strongly convex functions, provide gradient-variance and small-loss regret bounds, and establish first gradient-variation bounds for one-point bandit linear optimization and dynamic regret.

problem: Diffusion LLMs support arbitrary-order generation but performance critically depends on unmasking order, and existing strategies rely on greedy heuristics providing limited guidance.
approach: Path log-likelihood (Path LL) provides a trajectory-conditioned objective correlating with accuracy, enabling POKE-SMC, an efficient Sequential Monte Carlo-based framework that predicts future Path LL via lookahead value estimation.
contribution: POKE-SMC consistently improves accuracy by 2-3% on reasoning tasks over decoding-time scaling baselines at comparable inference overhead.

problem: InfoNCE underlying modern contrastive learning has its geometric mechanisms under-characterized beyond canonical alignment-uniformity decomposition, particularly for multimodal cases.
approach: A measure-theoretic framework tracks how representation measures evolve on an embedding manifold, proving value and gradient consistency and revealing geometric bifurcation between unimodal (convex) and symmetric multimodal (cross-coupled) regimes.
contribution: Results show entropy acts as a tie-breaker in unimodal case while multimodal case has persistent negative divergence, revealing that pairwise alignment alone cannot control cross-modal marginal structure.

problem: Black-box optimization methods including Evolution Strategies, Consensus-Based Optimization, and Optimization via Integration have been studied independently with unclear connections.
approach: A unified theoretical framework reveals methods differ in two design choices: fitness aggregation (controlling sharpness preference) and consensus scope (controlling modality), enabling construction of hybrid optimizers.
contribution: Hybrid optimizers (ES-OVI and CBO-OVI) enable control over flat-minima preference and achieve competitive results on language model merging and locomotion tasks with limited budgets.

problem: Model-based offline RL methods rely on heuristic uncertainty estimation for conservatism which can be unreliable, and avoiding artificial conservatism while maintaining data efficiency remains challenging.
approach: VIPO incorporates self-supervised feedback from value estimation to enhance model training by minimizing inconsistency between values learned from offline data and values estimated via the learned model.
contribution: VIPO achieves state-of-the-art performance on almost all D4RL and NeoRL benchmarks and provides a general framework integrable into existing model-based offline RL algorithms.

problem: Sparse autoencoders assume features combine additively through linear reconstruction, failing to capture compositional structure where compound concepts should decompose into interpretable constituents.
approach: PolySAE extends the SAE decoder with higher-order polynomial terms to model pairwise and triple feature interactions while preserving the linear encoder, using low-rank tensor factorization on a shared projection subspace.
contribution: PolySAE improves probing F1 by ~8% while maintaining comparable reconstruction, produces 2-10x larger class-conditional feature distribution distances, and shows interaction weights exhibit negligible correlation with co-occurrence (r=0.06 vs r=0.82 for SAE).

problem: LLM evaluations conflate benchmark performance with intrinsic capability, overlooking that observed outcomes arise from the entire evaluation system and that evaluation choices alone can induce 70% accuracy swings.
approach: LLM evaluatology grounds evaluation in causally motivated system design combining structured causal modeling with factorial decomposition under design of experiments, quantifying main and interaction effects via instance-level interventions.
contribution: The framework enables more interpretable, reproducible, and carefully attributed assessment of model capability by probing dataset-induced effects and jointly modeling evaluation components.

problem: Time-series forecasters typically map history to target via one-way inference and overlook structural information from how trajectories evolve after the target period.
approach: KUP-BI distills continuation-style knowledge from a train-only historical library to approximate post-target continuation and integrates it via lightweight feature-level gating, providing structured inductive bias.
contribution: KUP-BI consistently improves forecasting performance of state-of-the-art backbones on six public datasets without introducing information beyond training trajectories.

problem: Continual pre-training for domain adaptation involves substantial model changes but the underlying spectral dynamics and which components drive adaptation remain unclear.
approach: Spectral analysis via singular value decomposition reveals CPT leaves singular value spectra largely invariant with adaptation driven by singular vector changes, identifying domain-dependent head heterogeneity via head importance criterion.
contribution: Up to 60% of head updates can be removed without quality loss; selectively rewinding low-importance heads improves accuracy by up to 4%, and domain connectivity enables smooth interpolation between CPT checkpoints.

problem: Existing image editing models often produce unwanted changes in unintended regions while focusing on editing effects, failing to maintain content consistency.
approach: CoCoEdit uses region-regularized reinforcement learning with pixel-level similarity rewards complementing MLLM-based rewards and region-based regularization to preserve non-edited regions while encouraging editing effects.
contribution: CoCoEdit achieves superior editing quality and significantly better content consistency (measured by PSNR/SSIM and human ratings) compared to state-of-the-art models.
